channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: UK Could Hold Later Spending Review to Defer Decision on Defense
item.description: The UK government could publish a crucial spending plan in the second half of next year, despite expectations that it would be held in the spring or early summer.
item.dc:creator: Alex Wickham

item.title: Badenoch Downplays UK ‘Iron Dome’ Policy Under Funding Scrutiny
item.description: UK opposition leader Kemi Badenoch downplayed initial claims her plans for a £10 billion ($13.2 billion) air defense program would amount to a British “iron dome” after the proposal came under scrutiny.
item.dc:creator: Chloe Chaplain

item.title: Le Pen Vows to Cut French Deficit Below 3% to Court Investors
item.description: French presidential candidate Marine Le Pen, head of the far-right National Rally, proposed bringing the country’s deficit below 3% of GDP by 2032 at the latest in an ambitious new fiscal plan.
item.dc:creator: William Horobin, Jenny Che and Samy Adghirni

item.title: Turkish Politician Asked to Return Gains in Fund Crisis, AA Says
item.description: Turkish prosecutors asked lenders to hand over assets of the ruling party’s former deputy chair in the course of a funds-rout investigation that’s reached the top of President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s political establishment.
item.dc:creator: Tugce Ozsoy

item.title: Saudi-Led Forces Claim Yemen Ground Advances Against Houthis
item.description: Yemen’s internationally-recognized government, backed by Saudi Arabia, claimed to have regained territory from the Houthis, as fighting in the region near the Bab el-Mandeb strait intensifies.
item.dc:creator: Sherif Tarek and Ahmed Elimam

item.title: France Protests Go Nationwide & Europe Gets Tough on China
item.description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from Brussels, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.
On today's show, global stocks edged toward record highs as investors shrugged off concerns about elevated oil prices and bond yields near multi-decade highs.
Student protests in France are gaining momentum, with hundreds of high schools closed as teacher unions join the movement demanding more money for education.
And Germany and France are urging the European Union to adopt new powers that could exclude China from its single market, as the bloc’s two biggest economies adopt a more confrontational stance ahead of talks in Beijing.
Today's guest: Vincent Juvyns, ING Belgium, Chief Investment Strategist. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Singapore Refers Eight Public Officers to Police After Reviewing Property Deals
item.description: Singapore has referred cases involving eight public officers to the police after reviewing property purchases by officials who worked at agencies involved in rail planning, Coordinating Minister for Public Services Chan Chun Sing told parliament on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Srinidhi Ragavendran

item.title: Yemen Regains City of Mocha on Red Sea
item.description: Yemen's armed forces took control of the Red Sea city of Mocha on Monday after battles with the Iran-backed Houthis, state-run Saba said. This puts the internationally recognized government closer to taking over the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a narrow chokepoint between the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden that Saudi Arabia had been using to export oil and bypass the Strait of Hormuz. Bloomberg's Stuart Livingstone-Wallace reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: German Government in Danger as Parties Fight Over Tax Hikes
item.description: Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s government is struggling to agree on a package of measures to contain Germany’s widening budget gap in a growing dispute that’s becoming a danger to the coalition’s survival.
item.dc:creator: Kamil Kowalcze

item.title: Malaysia Repatriations to Myanmar Top 10,000 as Anwar Prepares to Host President
item.description: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said more than 10,000 people have been repatriated to Myanmar this year and he will raise the issue of sending more home when he meets Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing this week.
item.dc:creator: Danial Azhar and Kok Leong Chan

item.title: French Student Unrest Spreads as Teachers Also Walk Out
item.description: Hundreds of French high schools will shut Tuesday as teacher unions join a student-led protest movement demanding more money for education.
item.dc:creator: Benoit Berthelot and William Horobin

item.title: Supreme Court’s Alito Says Democratic Senate Win Won’t Prompt Him to Retire
item.description: Justice Samuel Alito said he plans to remain on the Supreme Court even if Democrats capture the Senate in next month’s midterms, dismissing speculation that he might quickly retire to ensure Donald Trump can get a successor confirmed.
item.dc:creator: Greg Stohr

item.title: India Police Halt Opposition March in Heavily Guarded Delhi
item.description: Police stopped opposition lawmakers from marching to India’s Election Commission on Tuesday as they demanded the resignation of the country’s top poll official, escalating a political confrontation over a contentious revision of voter rolls.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Roy

item.title: Takaichi Defends Absence From G7 Online Call After Criticism
item.description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi defended her absence from a Group of Seven online meeting, responding over social media to some critics who questioned why she didn’t attend despite her apparently free schedule.
item.dc:creator: Sakura Murakami

item.title: Quebec Separatists Win Power in New Challenge for Canada’s Carney
item.description: Voters in Quebec elected the separatist Parti Québécois for the first time in more than a decade, setting the stage for more strained relations with Prime Minister Mark Carney’s government and an eventual referendum on the province’s independence from Canada.
item.dc:creator: Mathieu Dion

item.title: Trump Eases Limits on Dyed Diesel in Bid to Cut Fuel Costs
item.description: President Donald Trump on Monday signed an executive order to ease restrictions on the use of a tax-exempt variety of diesel, his latest bid to pare costs for the fuel ahead of November’s midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Hadriana Lowenkron, Jennifer A. Dlouhy and Josh Wingrove

item.title: Tensions Flare as Kosovo Edges Toward Its Fourth Snap Vote
item.description: Tensions flared in Kosovo as protesters demanded lawmakers give their final approval to changes that would limit the powers of the country’s Hague-based war crimes court.
item.dc:creator: Gresa Kraja

item.title: Spain’s Sánchez Calls Snap Election After Housing Plan Fails
item.description:
Spain’s Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called a snap election after parliament rejected his plan to intervene in the housing market, amid demonstrations across Spain.
It’s the latest in a series of crises for his minority government, as Daniel Basteiro explains. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Sánchez Targets Toughest Comeback Yet With Early Spain Vote
item.description: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has a history of proving his critics wrong. But his decision Monday to call a snap election in the midst of a housing affordability crisis may be his most precarious political move to date.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Basteiro

item.title: Germany, France Push New Trade Weapon Before EU-China Talks
item.description: Germany and France are urging the European Union to adopt new powers that could sever China or other countries from its single market, as the bloc’s two biggest economies adopt a more confrontational stance ahead of talks in Beijing.
item.dc:creator: Arne Delfs and Jorge Valero
